item: One unreadable link or sitemap loc no longer ends a source's crawl, and a sitemap's page locs are held to the source's host (R626, R627)
refs: R626 R627 R624 R630 PR pending
summary: R626 and R627 (Plan's rulings on two findings of R624's read, one PR after R624). BEFORE: urllib.parse raises a bare ValueError on an href or loc such as http://[::1 (an unclosed IPv6 bracket), a stray ']', a bracketed host that is no address (http://[foo]/) or a netloc NFKC would change. src/ingest/crawl.py _harvest_links let it out of urljoin, which ended the whole crawl of the source; discover_sitemap_urls let it out of urlparse(sm_url) in the child check (index children and robots-declared sitemaps alike), which ended the whole discovery; and a urlset's page locs were handed on unread, so the caller's ingest_url raised it from EthicalFetcher.fetch and the walk of the rest of the sitemap's pages ended (the crawl rung logged the source as failed and rolled it back, the qualification trial counted an error). And a urlset's page locs were never host-checked (only child sitemaps were), so a sitemap could make the app fetch pages on other sites and store them as the source's. NOW: _harvest_links (crawl.py:137) skips an href it cannot read and hands it back; crawl_source counts the distinct ones over the whole crawl (crawl.py:238, :264) in CrawlReport.skipped_unreadable, also in to_dict (crawl.py:103, :112). Both checks in discover_sitemap_urls call ONE comparison, _off_host (sitemap.py:153): None when urlparse cannot read the URL, else the child sitemaps' rule, _registrable_host(netloc) != base_host. An unreadable child or page loc is counted in SitemapDiscoveryReport.skipped_unreadable (sitemap.py:206, :257, :298); an off-host page loc goes to skipped_off_host, written through failure_url (sitemap.py:296-301), and is never returned. Page locs are de-duplicated before the check, so each distinct loc is counted once. The other parses on these paths were gone through and never raise: _registrable_host and the host key catch the ValueError of .port, canonicalize_url catches everything, a link that reaches the fetcher has been read by urlparse already, and a URL urlparse reads but the fetcher cannot (a port out of range) is refused by the fetcher before any request, as before (a crawl tallies it fetch_failed). R627's EFFECT ('same rule' is the host minus www., not the registrable domain), from the bundled catalogues (6,731 sources in configs/sources.yml, academic_sources.yml, legal_sources_generated.yml, sources_spectrum.yml, official_sources.yml; none names a sitemap, they are found at run time): 906 have a domain that is itself a subdomain (edition.cnn.com, english.elpais.com, asia.nikkei.com, folha.uol.com.br, news.sky.com), whose sitemap pages on the parent domain or a sibling are now skipped; 78 (some among those 906) have a feed on a non-infrastructure subdomain of their own domain (kyodonews.net to english.kyodonews.net, yna.co.kr to en.yna.co.kr, radio-canada.ca to ici.radio-canada.ca, m.radiochisinau.md to radiochisinau.md, english.vov.vn to vov.vn, 22 erudit.org journals to www.erudit.org), the likeliest to list pages on another host of their domain; 3 have a Unicode domain (åa.no and two others), and _registrable_host does not IDNA-encode, so their pages written in punycode are off the host; the 29 statistics agencies all match. No existing test lists a page off its source's host (test_sitemap, test_crawl_supplement, test_stop_is_not_an_outcome, R624's), so none changed. The crawl's own link check already refused every one of these, so the sitemap and the crawl now agree. TESTS: tests/test_sitemap_scope_unreadable_r626_r627.py, 64, through the real crawl_source, discover_sitemap_urls, sitemap_trial_ingest and the crawl rung (_lane_step_crawl) with a real EthicalFetcher over an in-memory session (every planted off-site page routed, so a fetch is seen). 37 fail on local/r624 4c28b7e74: seven unreadable hrefs among good links (the good ones crawled, the bad one counted), a count once per crawl and on a page that is no article, seven unreadable page locs and seven unreadable index children, an unreadable robots-declared sitemap, five off-host page locs (another host, the source's name as a label, a suffix, a userinfo before the last @ listed masked, an IPv6 literal), the same off-host loc listed once and the same unreadable loc counted once, a subdomain page loc, a loc with no host, the Unicode/punycode case, the trial walking past an unreadable loc and never fetching an off-host one, and the crawl rung crawling the source (it failed it before). 27 pass there, all controls: a bracket in a relative path followed, a port out of range never requested and never ending the crawl or the trial, a page of readable links, the helpers never raising on any case, the source host however spelled (www., capitals, :443, :8443, http, an @ in the path or query), a www. source keeping its bare-host pages, an off-host child still listed and never fetched. 16 mutants, none survived (the harvest guard, the href not recorded, the page's set not gathered, the count not written, to_dict without it, a count per page; _off_host's guard, each check's skip and count, the page check undone, off-host page locs kept, the raw loc listed, the de-dup only for kept locs, the netloc compared by hand). 1,895 passed across the crawl, sitemap, R620/R621/R624, SSRF, network-consent, sink-sweep, repo-invariants and every other test that drives crawl or sitemap; the one failure (test_shared_file_writes: src/ingest/__init__.py:416/548/712) fails the same on 4c28b7e74. NOT CHANGED: the counts live on the two report objects only, where skipped_off_host already was: nothing reads skipped_off_host into an API response, a log line or the UI (the crawl rung reads urls and pages_fetched; the trial's result, which carries discovered/attempted/tally/errors, is discarded by qualification.py:1754; archive_backfill.py reads urls), so no chrome string was added. The off-host entries and the error lines are written through failure_url (R624's fold). After R624 and R630 are merged in, _off_host calls R624's _off_site, so a child sitemap or a page loc whose netloc holds an @ is off the host on both checks (R630), and crawl_source skips a harvested link carrying a userinfo before its scope check, whatever the scope (R630). The RSS feed pass had the same bug one layer down, found by this build: ingest_source (pipeline.py:633) hands an item link such as http://[::1 (feedparser passes it through, checked) to ingest_url, and EthicalFetcher.fetch's own urlparse (src/ingest/__init__.py) raised the bare ValueError, ending that source's feed pass. fetch() now refuses such a URL as an unsupported or malformed URL (FetchFailed, raised outside the handler, nothing requested), which ingest_url records as that item's failure; it covers every caller of fetch(). 9 tests: each of the 7 unreadable forms refused with nothing requested, a feed with an unreadable link between two good ones stores both, and a control (an ftp URL refused as before); 8 fail on the parent commit, the control passes; two mutants (the None not refused; the ValueError re-raised) killed. An unreadable crawl start URL or source domain still raises (configuration, not the host's text; the rung isolates it per source). By reading, not run: for a Unicode-domain source the crawl's own links read as off the site too (requests sends and answers the punycode host). Release-notes line: «A sitemap no longer widens a source's scope: pages it lists on other sites are skipped and counted, like its child sitemaps. One unreadable link on a page, in a sitemap or in a feed no longer ends that source's whole collection; it is skipped and counted. (R626, R627)»
